description: Worked example composing execution-join-ref-v1's post_commit_consistency invariant (PR#137, 2026-10-18) onto the request_occurrence/task/execution-receipt shape frozen in ogasurfproject-jpg/horizon-shield#51 (pilot scoping, 2026-10-18) and defined in COMPANION_v0.md / PILOT_v0.md at commit 4d720ace (MIT). This is NOT an alternative implementation of authority, payment, or acceptance -- those three roles are covered by MUSUBI/APS (authority_and_payment) and babyblueviper1's work-acceptance-record (acceptance) in the pilot itself, and are declared here, not recomputed. The only invariant this worked example computes is post_commit_consistency: does a LATER, independent observation of the audited output (the JCCDB cost database snapshot, or the deliverable) still match the response_sha256 the execution-receipt committed to at settlement time? Case A (within/paid/accepted, matches the pilot's own happy path) shows the new invariant does not interfere with it. Case D (new, proposed) is the gap after A closes validly: the JCCDB snapshot the estimate was audited against changes after acceptance. The original request/execution/payment/acceptance records remain exactly as valid as they were -- nobody misstated anything at settlement time -- a separate, later post_commit_observation names the divergence without collapsing the two into one state, the same principle execution-join-ref-v1's own post-commit-divergence-001 demonstrates.

vectors.description: Analogue of the pilot's own Case A (within/paid/accepted). authority_and_payment and acceptance are declared true (out of scope for this worked example -- MUSUBI/APS and invinoveritas's job). post_commit_consistency is computed: the post_commit_observation's observed_hash matches the execution-receipt's response_sha256 exactly, demonstrating the new invariant does not break the happy path.

Proposed Case D: the gap after Case A already closed validly. Same request_occurrence, task, and execution_receipt as Case A -- the original call was genuinely within, paid, and accepted; authority_and_payment and acceptance stay declared true, unaffected. ~24h later, an independent post_commit_observation recomputes the JCCDB cost database snapshot the estimate was audited against (same original fixture_quote_sha256, different jccdb_snapshot_sha256) and gets a different response_sha256 than the one the execution-receipt committed to at settlement. post_commit_consistency fails -- POST_COMMIT_DIVERGENCE -- while every other invariant, including the original execution-receipt's own validity, remains true. Nothing about the original call was ever false; the database it was checked against moved afterward.
vectors.failure_detail: execution_receipt.outcome.response_sha256=f15c6e0cd0bc… (committed at seen_block.height=920000). post_commit_observation at observed_at_ms=1783386400000 (~24h later) recomputes response_sha256=4f7cd5302242… for the same request_sha256=4edaf6c7461a… -- same fixture_quote_sha256, different jccdb_snapshot_sha256. The cost database the estimate was audited against changed after acceptance; the original acceptance was not wrong when it was made.
